passages.text: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Some time passed.
Absalom prepared a chariot for himself.
He also got horses for himself.
He arranged for fifty men to run in front of him.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לוֹ֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מֶרְכָּבָ֖ה וְסֻסִ֑ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,” Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom got up early every day.
He stood beside the road that led to the city gate.
Many people in Israel had disputes or complaints.
These people wanted the king to judge their cases.
Whenever someone came with a grievance for the king,
Absalom called out to that person.
He asked, “What city are you from?”
If the person answered, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”
Absalom said, “Look, your claims are good and right.
But the king has no deputy to hear you.”
passages.original: וְהִשְׁכִּים֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם וְעָמַ֕ד עַל־ יַ֖ד דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיְהִ֡י כָּל־ הָאִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִהְיֶה־ לּוֹ־ רִיב֩ לָב֨וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְשָׁל֤וֹם אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵֽי־ מִזֶּ֥ה עִיר֙ אַ֔תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מֵאַחַ֥ד שִׁבְטֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם רְאֵ֥ה דְבָרֶ֖ךָ טוֹבִ֣ים וּנְכֹחִ֑ים וְשֹׁמֵ֥עַ אֵין־ לְךָ֖ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom wanted power and influence in Israel.
Absalom spoke to the people at the city gate.
Absalom said, “If only someone would make me judge in the land.”
He said, “Then every person with a grievance or dispute could come to me.”
He said, “I would give each person justice.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִי־ יְשִׂמֵ֥נִי שֹׁפֵ֖ט בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְעָלַ֗י יָב֥וֹא כָּל־ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִהְיֶה־ לּוֹ־ רִ֥יב וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וְהִצְדַּקְתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom stood by the road at the city gate.
People came to Absalom with their problems.
When anyone came near Absalom to bow down to him, he acted kindly.
Absalom reached out his hand to the person.
He took hold of the person.
He kissed the person.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בִּקְרָב־ אִ֔ישׁ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת ל֑וֹ וְשָׁלַ֧ח אֶת־ יָד֛וֹ וְהֶחֱזִ֥יק ל֖וֹ וְנָ֥שַׁק לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom acted in a certain way toward the people of Israel.
Many Israelites came to the king for justice.
Absalom did these things to every Israelite who came for judgment.
He treated them kindly.
He listened to their problems.
He showed them favor.
He won their trust.
Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ יָבֹ֥אוּ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְגַנֵּב֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אֶת־ לֵ֖ב אַנְשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Four years passed.
Absalom spoke to the king.
Absalom said, “Please let me go to Hebron.
I want to fulfill a vow I made to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֛ם אֶת־ נִדְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ נָדַ֥רְתִּי לַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom spoke to the king.
Absalom said he had made a vow.
He made this vow while he lived in Geshur, in the land of Aram.
Absalom said, “If the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.”
passages.original: כִּי־ נֵ֙דֶר֙ נָדַ֣ר עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּשִׁבְתִּ֥י בִגְשׁ֛וּר בַּאֲרָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־ יָשִׁיב יְשִׁיבֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְעָבַדְתִּ֖י אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Absalom.
The king said, “Go in peace.”
Absalom stood up.
Absalom left.
Absalom went to Hebron.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵ֣ךְ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ חֶבְרֽוֹנָה׃פ

passages.text: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom wanted to become king.
Absalom sent spies to every tribe of Israel.
He gave the spies a message to deliver.
He told them, “When you hear the sound of the horn, say this: ‘Absalom is king in Hebron.’”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ מְרַגְּלִ֔ים בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּשָׁמְעֲכֶם֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מָלַ֥ךְ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Two hundred men went with Absalom.
These men came from Jerusalem.
Absalom invited them as guests.
They followed Absalom.
They acted innocently.
They did not know anything about Absalom’s plan.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם הָלְכ֞וּ מָאתַ֤יִם אִישׁ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קְרֻאִ֖ים וְהֹלְכִ֣ים לְתֻמָּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כָּל־ דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom wanted to take the throne from his father David.
Absalom offered sacrifices.
While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel.
Ahithophel was from the town of Giloh.
Ahithophel was a counselor to King David.
Absalom called Ahithophel to join him.
The conspiracy against David became stronger.
More and more people followed Absalom.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אַ֠בְשָׁלוֹם אֶת־ אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל הַגִּֽילֹנִ֜י יוֹעֵ֣ץ דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִגִּלֹ֔ה בְּזָבְח֖וֹ אֶת־ הַזְּבָחִ֑ים וַיְהִ֤י הַקֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ אַמִּ֔ץ וְהָעָ֛ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָרָ֖ב אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
passages.sermon: A messenger came to David.\r\nThe messenger spoke to David.\r\nThe messenger said, “The men of Israel support Absalom.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּגִּ֔יד אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הָיָ֛ה לֶב־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king in Jerusalem.
Absalom was his son.
Absalom started a rebellion against David.
David spoke to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem.
David said, “Get up.
Let us run away.
If we do not leave, we will not escape from Absalom.
We must hurry and go now.
If we wait, Absalom will come quickly.
He will catch us.
He will bring disaster upon us.
He will strike the city with the sword.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּ֠וִד לְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֨יו אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֤וֹ בִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ ק֣וּמוּ וְנִבְרָ֔חָה כִּ֛י לֹא־ תִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥נוּ פְלֵיטָ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם מַהֲר֣וּ לָלֶ֗כֶת פֶּן־ יְמַהֵ֤ר וְהִשִּׂגָ֙נוּ֙ וְהִדִּ֤יחַ עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וְהִכָּ֥ה הָעִ֖יר לְפִי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David’s servants spoke to him.
They said, “You are our lord and king.”
They said, “We are your servants.”
They said, “We will do whatever you choose.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֛ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.
passages.sermon:
King David was in Jerusalem.
Absalom, his son, was threatening him.
David decided to leave the city.
David set out on foot.
His entire household followed him.
David left ten concubines behind.
He told them to take care of the palace.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ בֵּית֖וֹ בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֵ֣ת עֶ֧שֶׂר נָשִׁ֛ים פִּֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֥ר הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house, and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
passages.sermon:
King David left the city.
All the people followed King David on foot.
King David stopped at the last house.
All King David’s servants passed by him.
The Cherethites passed by King David.
The Pelethites passed by King David.
Six hundred Gittites also passed by King David.
These Gittites had come with King David from Gath.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּרְחָֽק׃ וְכָל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ עֹבְרִ֣ים עַל־ יָד֔וֹ וְכָל־ הַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְכָל־ הַפְּלֵתִ֑י וְכָֽל־ הַגִּתִּ֞ים שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֤אוּ בְרַגְלוֹ֙ מִגַּ֔ת עֹבְרִ֖ים עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ittai the Gittite.
David was the king of Israel.
Ittai was from Gath.
Ittai was not an Israelite.
Ittai was a foreigner.
Ittai was also an exile from his homeland.
David said, “Why do you want to go with us?”
David told Ittai, “Go back.”
David told Ittai, “Stay with the new king.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֔י לָ֧מָּה תֵלֵ֛ךְ גַּם־ אַתָּ֖ה אִתָּ֑נוּ שׁ֣וּב וְשֵׁ֤ב עִם־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ כִּֽי־ נָכְרִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וְגַם־ גֹּלֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה לִמְקוֹמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Ittai the Gittite.
Ittai was a foreigner.
Ittai had just arrived the day before.
David said, “You came only yesterday.
Should I make you wander with us today?
I do not know where I am going.
Go back.
Take your brothers with you.
May the LORD show you kindness and faithfulness.”
passages.original: תְּמ֣וֹל׀ בּוֹאֶ֗ךָ וְהַיּ֞וֹם אֲנוֹעֲךָ עִמָּ֙נוּ֙ לָלֶ֔כֶת וַאֲנִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ אֲנִ֖י הוֹלֵ֑ךְ שׁ֣וּב וְהָשֵׁ֧ב אֶת־ אַחֶ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃

passages.text: But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”
passages.sermon:
Ittai was a foreigner and an exile.
Ittai spoke to King David.
Ittai said, "As surely as the LORD lives."
Ittai said, "As surely as my lord the king lives."
Ittai said, "Wherever my lord the king is, I will be there."
Ittai said, "If it means death, I will be there."
Ittai said, "If it means life, I will be there."
Ittai said, "Your servant will be with you."
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן אִתַּ֛י אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה וְחֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֠י אִם־ בִּמְק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽהְיֶה־ שָּׁ֣ם׀ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִם־ לְמָ֙וֶת֙ אִם־ לְחַיִּ֔ים כִּי־ שָׁ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: “March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Ittai was a Gittite and a foreigner.
David spoke to Ittai.
David said, “Go ahead and cross over.”
Ittai the Gittite obeyed David.
Ittai crossed over.
All his men crossed over with him.
All the little ones with Ittai also crossed over.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־ אִתַּ֖י לֵ֣ךְ וַעֲבֹ֑ר וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֞ר אִתַּ֤י הַגִּתִּי֙ וְכָל־ אֲנָשָׁ֔יו וְכָל־ הַטַּ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
The people in the countryside cried loudly.
All the people walked by.
The king crossed the Kidron Valley.
All the people went past him.
They walked toward the road to the wilderness.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ בּוֹכִים֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם עֹֽבְרִ֑ים וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹבֵר֙ בְּנַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ עֹבְרִ֔ים עַל־ פְּנֵי־ דֶ֖רֶךְ אֶת־ הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until the people had passed out of the city.
passages.sermon:
Zadok was present.
All the Levites were with Zadok.
The Levites carried the ark of the covenant of God.
They set down the ark of God.
Abiathar offered sacrifices.
Abiathar continued until all the people had left the city.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֨ה גַם־ צָד֜וֹק וְכָֽל־ הַלְוִיִּ֣ם אִתּ֗וֹ נֹֽשְׂאִים֙ אֶת־ אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֙קוּ֙ אֶת־ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּ֖עַל אֶבְיָתָ֑ר עַד־ תֹּ֥ם כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם לַעֲב֥וֹר מִן־ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Zadok.
The king said, “Return the ark of God to the city.
If the LORD looks on me with favor, He will bring me back.
He will let me see the ark again.
He will let me see His dwelling place again.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְצָד֔וֹק הָשֵׁ֛ב אֶת־ אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הָעִ֑יר אִם־ אֶמְצָ֥א חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֶהֱשִׁבַ֕נִי וְהִרְאַ֥נִי אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־ נָוֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Zadok the priest.
David trusted God.
David said, “If God says, ‘I do not delight in you,’ I am here.
Let God do to me what is good in His eyes.”
passages.original: וְאִם֙ כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֔ר לֹ֥א חָפַ֖צְתִּי בָּ֑ךְ הִנְנִ֕י יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Zadok the priest.
David called Zadok a seer.
David told Zadok to return to the city in peace.
David told Zadok to take his son Ahimaaz with him.
David told Abiathar to take his son Jonathan with him.
David told both priests to take their sons and go back to the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֔ן הֲרוֹאֶ֣ה אַתָּ֔ה שֻׁ֥בָה הָעִ֖יר בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וַאֲחִימַ֨עַץ בִּנְךָ֜ וִיהוֹנָתָ֧ן בֶּן־ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר שְׁנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Zadok the priest.
David said, “Look at me.
I will wait at the fords of the wilderness.
I will stay there.
I will wait until you send me a message.
I will wait until you tell me what is happening.”
passages.original: רְאוּ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י מִתְמַהְמֵ֔הַּ בְּעַבְרוֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַ֣ד בּ֥וֹא דָבָ֛ר מֵעִמָּכֶ֖ם לְהַגִּ֥יד לִֽי׃

passages.text: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.
passages.sermon:
Zadok was a priest.
Abiathar was also a priest.
Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God.
They brought the ark of God back to Jerusalem.
Zadok and Abiathar stayed in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨שֶׁב צָד֧וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת־ אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David walked up the Mount of Olives.
David was weeping as he went up.
David covered his head.
David walked barefoot.
All the people with David went with him.
Each person covered his own head.
All the people went up the mountain.
All the people wept as they went.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֡ד עֹלֶה֩ בְמַעֲלֵ֨ה הַזֵּיתִ֜ים עֹלֶ֣ה׀ וּבוֹכֶ֗ה וְרֹ֥אשׁ לוֹ֙ חָפ֔וּי וְה֖וּא הֹלֵ֣ךְ יָחֵ֑ף וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֗וֹ חָפוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְעָל֥וּ עָלֹ֖ה וּבָכֹֽה׃

passages.text: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Someone came to David.
The person gave David news.
He said, “Ahithophel is with the conspirators.”
Ahithophel had joined Absalom.
Absalom was David’s son.
Absalom was rebelling against David.
David heard this news.
David prayed to God.
David said, “O LORD, make Ahithophel’s advice foolish.”
passages.original: וְדָוִד֙ הִגִּ֣יד לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲחִיתֹ֥פֶל בַּקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים עִם־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד סַכֶּל־ נָ֛א אֶת־ עֲצַ֥ת אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David came to the top of the Mount of Olives.
This was the place where David used to worship God.
Hushai was an Archite.
Hushai came to meet David at the summit.
Hushai had torn his robe.
Hushai had put dust on his head.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י דָוִד֙ בָּ֣א עַד־ הָרֹ֔אשׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֤ה לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י קָר֙וּעַ֙ כֻּתָּנְתּ֔וֹ וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
\r\nDavid spoke to Hushai the Archite.
\r\nDavid said, “If you come with me, you will be a burden to me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑ד אִ֚ם עָבַ֣רְתָּ אִתִּ֔י וְהָיִ֥תָ עָלַ֖י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃

passages.text: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Hushai, his friend.
David said, "You can help me."
You must return to the city.
You must speak to Absalom.
Say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king.'
Say, 'In the past, I served your father.'
Say, 'Now, I will serve you.'
If you do this, you will defeat the advice of Ahithophel for me.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הָעִ֣יר תָּשׁ֗וּב וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ עַבְדְּךָ֨ אֲנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֔ה עֶ֣בֶד אָבִ֤יךָ וַֽאֲנִי֙ מֵאָ֔ז וְעַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְהֵפַרְתָּ֣ה לִ֔י אֵ֖ת עֲצַ֥ת אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃

passages.text: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
passages.sermon:
Zadok and Abiathar are priests.
They will be there with you.
You will hear things from the king’s palace.
Tell Zadok and Abiathar the priests everything you hear.
passages.original: וַהֲל֤וֹא עִמְּךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם צָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּהֲנִ֑ים וְהָיָ֗ה כָּל־ הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּשְׁמַע֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תַּגִּ֕יד לְצָד֥וֹק וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

passages.text: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz is the son of Zadok.
Jonathan is the son of Abiathar.
Both sons are with Zadok and Abiathar.
You will hear news in the city.
Send all the news to me by Ahimaaz and Jonathan.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ שָׁ֤ם עִמָּם֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲחִימַ֣עַץ לְצָד֔וֹק וִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן לְאֶבְיָתָ֑ר וּשְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם בְּיָדָם֙ אֵלַ֔י כָּל־ דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
passages.sermon: Hushai was David’s friend.\r\nHushai came to the city of Jerusalem.\r\nAt the same time, Absalom entered Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א חוּשַׁ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד הָעִ֑יר וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יָבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
